outcome.technical: (1) _clause_coverage.py: _list_opens_under now returns (opens, at). The direct path (an opener numbered one right after the word) and the next-line path (an opener numbered one at the start of the next line holding text, outside a fence) are unchanged byte for byte in behaviour and return at=None. A new third path, _list_after_label, takes label words on the word's own line: the first opener numbered one after a blank opens a list only when an opener numbered two, the same way, follows after a blank later on the line or at the start of the next line holding text, outside a fence. It is one pass along the line, keeping the first one of each way. New helpers: _opener (number and way of an opener), _opener_on_line, _next_text_line (the existing blank-line walk, factored out). _markers stores where such a list opens as marker['list']; _read passes it to _read_body, which reads numbers from there as if it opened the line, so the label becomes the lead-in, as it already was across a line break. The strict column never takes the bare word, so marker['list'] is always None there and the strict reading is untouched. (2) tests/test__clause_coverage.py: new stage cw-same with cw14 (60 descriptions: 5 multi-word labels x 6 numbering forms x second item on the same or the next line; the wide count comes from the construction and equals the one-word twin's count, the parting line is the label's line), cw15 (allow: 7 prose lines with a single reference numbered one later in the line, a version number directly or after label words, a (1) followed by a (3)), and cw16 (allow: the word or label words, then a backtick or tilde fence whose first line is an opener numbered one). (3) Docs: the module docstring (SILENT ONLY ON AGREEMENT), the READING_CHOICES bare row, the _markers and acceptance_reading docstrings, manifest-conventions.md, the PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md _clause_coverage section and the Unreleased CHANGELOG entry now state the rule and its two limits (a bare label is read only over a list numbered from one; a reference numbered one directly after the word in prose is read as a list). Both limits were checked against the code: 'Acceptance (1) of the handbook says so.' prints 'finds 1 item'; '## Acceptance criteria' over '> 1.'/'> 2.', 'Acceptance criteria' over '**1.**', '2. a' and '(2) a (3) b' print nothing. (4) The fence check on the next-line path is unreachable, an equivalent mutant: a bare marker word is never inside a fence (_markers skips it), so the next line holding text after its line is outside every fence or is the fence's own opening line, and that line starts with backticks or tildes and so cannot match an opener. cw16 pins the behaviour, and the fence's opening line is what stops it today. No case can fail without the check, so Acceptance item 3 cannot be met as written. Mutation row 3 shows it: 88/88 green and 0 of 40210 descriptions differ. Row 4 shows cw16 goes red once a fenced line is reachable and the check is gone. Row 5 shows the check alone keeps cw16 green when the walk does reach the fenced line. cw15 and cw16 are allow cases and pass before and after; cw14 carries the red.
